newsitem.title: UK: UK's Cook says employment must balance EMU targets.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cook says employment must balance EMU targets.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Wednesday the monetary objectives of a single European currency should be balanced with broader economic objectives such as higher employment.

Speaking to a Trades Union Congress (TUC) conference on "Social Europe," he said the new Labour government supported the inclusion of an employment chapter in the European Union treaty at next month's Amsterdam summit.

"We will do so because we believe that it is very important that we should balance the monetary targets that are already in the treaty relating to the single currency with broader economic objectives such as higher levels of employment," Cook said.
"Progress towards achieving those monetary targets must be within an overall package that's aimed at creating jobs and must not be at the expense of employment."
Cook said he did not accept that signing up to the Social Chapter on workers' rights, which the new government plans to do, would damage the country's competitiveness, but added:
"We will carefully scrutinise all future directives to make sure that they will boost employment rather than hinder employment."
The new government wanted Britain to have a flexible labour force without unnecessary regulation, in which employees had access to good training to boost their skills.
"If we want to be competitive in the global economy, we will never do it on the basis of low skills, poor working conditions and dead-end careers," Cook said.
